_notes.change: Initial implementation. requireCodeOwnerReview=true enforces team reviewer requests via CODEOWNERS + this flag. The ruleset field required_reviewers is not available on the current GitHub plan.

Added 3 strict required checks for spark-match-02-infrastructure (tflint, gitleaks, sonar-terraform) after gap analysis revealed 3 PRs (#77/#78/#79) had bypassed tflint via admin-bypass. Tracked in tasks/devops/pending/sprint-2/03-strict-required-checks-and-admin-bypass-policy.md.

Reconciled spark-match-02-infrastructure statusChecks against actual reported check contexts. Manifest had 5 placeholder names (Plan (dev) / Plan (dev), tflint (env=dev), etc.) that did not match the 8 checks GitHub Actions actually reports (plan-dev / plan-, tflint / tflint-, etc.). Surfaced by --check returning drift. Fix: replaced 5 placeholders with the 8 real check contexts reported by /actions/runs/{id}/jobs API.

Added lint-commits / commitlint-main to required status checks for spark-match-01-devops. Defense against REST API merge pitfall: when squash-merging via PUT /pulls/N/merge without explicit commit_title, GitHub uses the PR title as the merge commit subject. If the PR title has camelCase, the resulting merge commit violates subject-case in commitlint, but the PR-side commitlint check (which lints git commit messages, not PR title) had already passed. Adding commitlint-main as required catches this on the post-merge push to main.

Replaced lint-commits / commitlint-main with lint-commits / commitlint, and made the job name in reusable-commitlint.yml static. The job was named commitlint-${{ head.ref || ref_name }}, so the published check context carried the branch name: commitlint-main only ever appeared on a push to main, never on a pull request. A required check that never reports leaves every PR stuck on 'Expected - Waiting for status to be reported', which forced an admin bypass on every merge - the exact thing the 2026-08-01 entry added strict checks to stop. The 2026-08-04 intent is not reachable this way regardless: required status checks gate the merge and are evaluated against the PR head SHA, so a check that only runs after the merge can never be a merge gate. The defense against the merge-commit-subject pitfall stays where it already worked, in the AGENTS.md section 4.5 checklist (validate the PR title, then pass commit_title and commit_message explicitly). The post-merge run still executes on main and still fails loudly if a bad subject lands.
